Identificativo prova: lfu Leggi il documento e restituisci i tre codici INIZIO, CENTRO e FINE. INIZIO: AMBRA-4729

Project Maya

GLM-5.3-Flash (321 B), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (748 B) and MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (428 B) on your own GPU
private and fast · one NVIDIA GPU or up to 16 · AMD and Windows (experimental) · chat, pictures, OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API · several requests at once

Created and led by Peasant Smith (@mw00), co-maintained with @needmorevram


Project Maya is free. If it runs well on your PC, sponsoring it pays for the test hardware and the work on it.

Models this size usually need a datacenter. Maya runs three of them on the hardware you already have: **GLM-5.3-Flash**, **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017** and **MiniMax-M3.1-Flash**. Each model has an architecture-specific path in the shared backend. It keeps the experts your conversation uses most on the GPU, the next ones in RAM and the rest on your NVMe SSD, and moves them as you chat. It measures your GPUs, CPU, RAM and SSD and tunes itself to them. Nothing leaves your machine. - **Fast:** up to 149 tokens/s on two RTX 5090s and an RTX 4090, 124 on two H100s, 118 on four RTX 4090s, 81 on one RTX PRO 6000, 30+ on a single RTX 5090. [Real numbers from real users](#how-fast-is-it). - **Close to the original:** Maya's own quants of GLM-5.3-Flash keep 97.7-99.2% of the FP8 model's zero-shot accuracy; DeepSeek V4.1 · Maya-S picks the same next token as the original 92.6% of the time, MiniMax M3.1 · Maya-S 87.6% (the average over its categories). - **Plugs into your tools:** OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API with tool calls, ready for coding agents. - **Several requests at once:** up to 8 answered together with GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and MiniMax-M3.1-Flash - for agents that run several sessions, or several people on one PC. - **Everything in the box:** a chat and a live monitor in the browser, pictures, thinking levels, a one-command setup. ## Quick start ```sh git clone https://github.com/mw00/project-maya.git && cd project-maya ./setup.sh ``` The setup asks which model you want, downloads it, builds everything once and **starts the model**. Then open `http://127.0.0.1:8080`. Windows: `START-MAYA.bat` instead of `./setup.sh`. More in [Install](#install). ## Pick your model Every Maya quant is named after its model, then its tier - XS, S, M or L, by how many bits its experts keep. The setup recommends one for your PC; to pick one yourself, give its setup id: `./setup.sh --model glm-maya-s24`. | Model | Maya quant · setup id | Size | Made for | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | | **[GLM-5.3-Flash](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash)**
zai-org · MIT · 321 B, 18 B active · up to 1M context | **Maya-S** (default) · `glm-maya-s` | 96.5 GB | PCs with a smaller memory pool (RAM and VRAM together) | | | Maya-S24 · `glm-maya-s24` | 94.7 GB | cards of 24 GB or less: ~1.5 GB more of the card for experts, decode +14% | | | Maya-M · `glm-maya-m` | 116 GB | a bigger memory pool; calibrated toward tool calls and front-end code | | | Maya-M-Derisked · `glm-maya-m-derisked` | 116 GB | Maya-M with a weight edit by [Blackfrost_AI](https://x.com/Blackfrost_AI) that reduces blanket refusals; experimental | | | Maya-L · `glm-maya-l` | 156.3 GB | the biggest memory pools; the closest to the original | | **[DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017)**
DeepSeek · MIT · 748 B | **Maya-S** (default) · `deepseek-maya-s` | 340 GB | any amount of memory: what VRAM and RAM don't hold is read from the SSD | | | Maya-XS · `deepseek-maya-xs` | 277 GB | the whole model in a 128 GB PC's memory (the Engram tables stay on the SSD) | | **[MiniMax-M3.1-Flash](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash)**
MiniMax · [MiniMax Community License](LICENSE.minimax-m31) · 428 B, 23 B active · up to 1M context | Maya-XS · `minimax-maya-xs` | 93 GB | the whole model in a 128 GB PC's memory | | | Maya-S · `minimax-maya-s` | 122 GB | closer to the original | All of them run on NVIDIA from the V100 / RTX 20 on, and on AMD and Windows (experimental; see [What you need](#what-you-need)). DeepSeek's sizes include its Engram tables. The setup also offers unsloth's GGUF and LibertAIDAI's EXL3 quants of DeepSeek, orcarouter's abliterated DeepSeek, Mia-AiLab's EXL3 quant of MiniMax, turboderp's EXL3 quants of GLM, and Qwen-3.8-Flash-Next (CYBER-FROST) as its Q5_K_M GGUF, with pictures ([its settings](docs/SETTINGS.md#qwen-38-flash-next-cyber-frost)). **Each model's files, drafters, pictures and options: [docs/MODELS.md](docs/MODELS.md).** ## Quality Maya's quants are made from each model's released weights and measured against the original: - **GLM-5.3 · Maya quants** keep 97.7-99.2% of the FP8 model's zero-shot accuracy and pick its next token 83-90% of the time (Maya-L: 99.2%, 90%). How they're made and measured: [MAYA-S](bench/results/MAYA-S.md), [MAYA-S24](bench/results/MAYA-S24.md), [MAYA-M](bench/results/MAYA-M.md), [MAYA-L](bench/results/MAYA-L.md). - **DeepSeek V4.1 · Maya-S** picks the same next token as the original 92.6% of the time. - **MiniMax M3.1 · Maya-S** picks it 87.6% of the time (the average over its categories). More on each model's card on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/peasantsmith). ## How fast is it? Real machines measured by our users, most with `./maya.sh --bench` (decode: three greedy 256-token answers; prefill: an 8K-token prompt unless the row says otherwise). Share yours: `--bench`, then `--report`, in a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/mw00/project-maya/issues).

The speed holds as a conversation grows, and the first answers after a start are the slowest while the caches fill with what you use. ## Using it - **In the browser:** chat (kept in your browser, with search, pins and folders, per-chat instructions and thinking level, edit and regenerate, HTML previews), a live **Monitor** of the model and your hardware (down to what fills each GPU's memory), a context size and port you can change in Settings, and **Models**: every model set up on this machine, switching to another (Maya starts again with it) and each one's engine settings (context, GPUs, drafting, images, memory), saved into its `maya-.json`. - **Saved:** the sidebar's Saved line adds up what the model's own API (DeepSeek's, Z.ai's or MiniMax's) would have charged for the same tokens - the prompt Maya reuses from its cache at the API's cached price, DeepSeek's peak hours at its peak price - kept per model in `token-savings.json`; its prices can be changed in **Settings › Savings**. - **Your apps and coding agents:** an OpenAI-compatible API at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1`, and Anthropic's at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/messages` (Claude Code: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080`). Tool calls are streamed as the model writes them, and a long prompt's reading progress too when a request asks for it (`"return_progress": true`). A web page served from another address can call it too once you allow its address (`"cors_origins"`, [docs/SETUP.md](docs/SETUP.md#web-pages-on-another-address)). - **Responses API:** `/v1/responses` supports text/image conversations, streaming, function tool calls, schema-validated output, background tasks with cancellation/replay, and optional shared in-memory history (`store:true`, `previous_response_id`). Responses are not stored by default. Options and limits: [docs/RESPONSES.md](docs/RESPONSES.md). - **Thinking:** Off, Low, High (the default) or Max, in Settings or per request. - **Pictures:** attach one in the chat, or send image parts through either API. - **From another device:** `./maya.sh --setup --host 0.0.0.0 --api-key `. Always set a key. - **Tuning:** `./maya.sh --calibrate` tunes the engine to your hardware in 10-15 minutes. Every setting: [docs/SETTINGS.md](docs/SETTINGS.md). - **Each model's own options** - GLM-5.3-Flash's several requests at once (`--parallel`), long contexts and DFlash2 drafter; DeepSeek's kept conversations, expert loading and Engram read-ahead; MiniMax's thinking levels: [docs/MODELS.md](docs/MODELS.md). # CENTRO: CEDRO-8361 # What you need | | | | --- | --- | | **GPU** | NVIDIA, compute capability 7.0 or newer (V100, RTX 20 and newer): one, or up to 16 that share the model. More VRAM is faster. Pascal (Tesla P40 / P100, GTX 10) is experimental, not validated yet. **AMD (experimental):** RX 7900 XT / XTX, Radeon AI PRO R9700 / RX 9070, Strix Halo and Gorgon Halo (Radeon 8060S / 8065S); RX 6800 / 6900 and Radeon PRO V620 / W6800 not validated yet; GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 read pictures there too - [docs/AMD_MAYA.md](docs/AMD_MAYA.md) | | **RAM** | 32 GB runs it. More RAM keeps more experts close and is faster | | **Disk** | **A fast NVMe SSD** with room for the model (~100 GB for GLM-5.3 · Maya-S, ~160 GB for GLM-5.3 · Maya-L, ~350 GB for DeepSeek V4.1 · Maya-S, ~520 GB for unsloth's GGUF of it, ~95 GB for MiniMax M3.1 · Maya-XS, ~200 GB for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash's EXL3 quant) and its picture encoder (1.1 GB). Not a hard disk | | **System** | Linux (x86-64; a CPU with AVX2 is best), the NVIDIA driver, CUDA 12.x (CUDA 13 works for RTX 20 and newer, not for the V100 or Pascal), g++, Python 3.10+. Windows 10/11 (experimental): [docs/WINDOWS.md](docs/WINDOWS.md). Not WSL2. AMD: ROCm 7 | The setup checks all of this, prints the exact command for anything missing, and installs nothing system-wide. ## Install Run the two commands in [Quick start](#quick-start) and answer a few questions (Enter takes the recommended choice). The setup shows every download before it starts it, builds everything once (20-40 minutes plus the download) and **starts the model**. Then open `http://127.0.0.1:8080`. Ctrl+C stops it, and `./setup.sh` starts it again right away. - **Windows:** `START-MAYA.bat` instead of `./setup.sh` - see [docs/WINDOWS.md](docs/WINDOWS.md). - **AMD:** [docs/AMD_MAYA.md](docs/AMD_MAYA.md). - **Mac with Apple Silicon (experimental, GLM-5.3-Flash):** `./maya.sh --backend metal` - see [docs/METAL.md](docs/METAL.md). Built and unit-tested on GitHub's Macs, not yet tested by us with the real model (we have no Mac): if you run it, please tell us how it went in an issue. - **Intel Arc:** not supported by Maya's engine; a community report of the Maya-XS DeepSeek GGUFs on llama.cpp's SYCL backend: [docs/INTEL_ARC.md](docs/INTEL_ARC.md). - **Updating:** the page's **Settings › About and updates**, or `git pull` then `./setup.sh`. The model isn't downloaded again. - **Model files downloaded another way** (a download manager, another PC, a Hugging Face cache): `./maya.sh --import-model FOLDER` finds Maya's files in FOLDER by size and checksum, whatever they are called, and moves them into place (`--copy` when FOLDER is on another drive; the originals stay). Files that do not match are left alone. - **Every option** (GPUs, context, a model folder you already have, remote access, ...): [docs/SETUP.md](docs/SETUP.md). > **The start takes a few minutes:** the engine pins most of the free RAM (all but about 6 GB) for its expert tier, > so other programs get little RAM while Maya runs. ## Something went wrong? Run **`./maya.sh --report`** (Windows: `START-MAYA.bat --report`) right after a slow answer or an error, and attach the `maya-report.txt` it writes to a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/mw00/project-maya/issues). It holds your hardware, your setup and the engine's speed lines; nothing is sent anywhere by itself. The engine's own log is `maya-.log` in the Maya folder. - **The build stops** ("nvcc ... cannot build for these GPUs", "unsupported GNU version", or `cuda_profiler_api.h` / `nvtx3/nvToolsExt.h` missing): [docs/SETUP.md](docs/SETUP.md#if-the-build-fails) has the fix for each. - **Slow, with the SSD busy all the time:** not enough free RAM for the experts. Close programs or add RAM. - **Windows: answers suddenly several times slower:** the card is too full and Windows moves GPU memory to RAM. Leave more of it free: `START-MAYA.bat --setup --vram-reserve-mib 2048` ([the expert pool's size](docs/SETTINGS.md#the-expert-pools-size)). - **Windows on a Strix Halo / Gorgon Halo: other programs run out of memory, or the setup warns about the page file:** set the page file to the size the setup prints ([docs/AMD_MAYA.md](docs/AMD_MAYA.md)). - **The download stopped:** run `./maya.sh` again; it continues where it stopped. - **Port 8080 is in use:** Maya is already running, or `--port 8081` starts another one. Against v1.1.41 on our test PCs, an 8K-token DeepSeek prompt read about 1.27x faster on one GPU and 1.1x faster with `--tp 2`; decode, and the other models' speeds, are unchanged. - **Pictures on every model and every build:** - GLM-5.3-Flash reads pictures on AMD GPUs - Linux and Windows, discrete cards and Ryzen AI Max APUs (#345, thanks @Ehco). The encoder's matmuls and attention now add up in float32 on the GPU, so its answers about a picture match the CPU encoder's on AMD (they drifted on a few image patches before) and on NVIDIA's newer cards too. - Qwen-3.8-Flash-Next (CYBER-FROST) reads pictures. The setup downloads its 0.9 GB image encoder (it asks first), and the encoder runs on the GPU in memory the engine lends it while a picture is read: on an 8 GB card the expert cache and, if need be, the draft layer's experts are lent and read back afterwards. On an 8 GB card a picture is read about 3.6x faster than with the CPU encoder; text answers before and after a picture are the same. - DeepSeek reads pictures with the EXL3 quants on V100s too, and the setup says why a PC short of RAM reads text only. A fresh 20-30K-token prompt read 16-24% faster on one and on two GPUs in our tests, with the same output. On our RAM-limited test (32 GB, one GPU) a long answer took about 20% less time, with the later part about 2x faster, and the same tokens. `--mmap-experts auto` (the default) is unchanged. `DS4_COPY_FAIR=0` restores the old order. - **Agents:** - The loop guard now works across turns (#640, thanks @merbanan): an agent that makes the same tool call with the same result a third time gets a short note in its prompt, and one that keeps going is steered off it. Normal agent conversations, and a call repeated after an edit, get exactly the same prompt as before. On by default. - GLM: a cancelled prompt read keeps its last checkpoint, so an agent that times out and retries goes on from there instead of reading the whole prompt again (#573, thanks @rushisan). Keeping the snapshot before the generation prompt, so a cancelled answer's next prompt continues it, is opt-in for now (`MAYA_GLM_SNAP_GEN=1`, #572, thanks @rushisan). - Very long streamed tool arguments no longer slow down as they grow, and streamed replies are sent without delay (#626, thanks @SeriousRising). - **Server and clients:** - Open WebUI's Models page can load the model, free its GPU memory and watch its state through llama.cpp's `/models/load`, `/models/unload` and `/models/sse` - off unless `"model_management": true` is in the config (#678, thanks @rilken-star). - `/v1/models` lists each model's `context_length` for clients that size their requests by it (#649, thanks @NorwinYu). - `/status` asks for the API key when one is set, and a request during an engine start gets a retryable 503 (#677, thanks @rilken-star).
